chapter: Venues, circuits and the music business
title: Same conditions in Europe
summary: Clubs in Europe follow the same tradition, even in basement bomb shelters.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Do you find this is different in other countries?

No. They follow the same tradition in Europe. I remember seeing a great musician, I forget, he was a blues singer-player. I'll remember in a minute. He was -- we were in the second or third basement, a place that used -- they used to use for bomb shelter. Yeah. Somehow this is supposed to be sexy and inspiring, that we're in the corner in the dark in the basement where you can -- if a fire happened, we're lucky nobody was toasted because a lot of these joints are in the basement. No. If it was up to me, I would finish them off, but it's not, and the musicians get a chance, the young musicians and singers get a chance to entertain and test their instruments and things, but I'll be glad when it's different. I'm jealous when I see ballet dancers in their settings and classical musicians in their settings. That's when you bring your best, not when you're in a smoky dark funky room without a dressing room. Okay. I ranted and railed about that.
